title: Val ruler leaks: select on novel-span words (Sherlock1+TheMoth), drop MOCHA
description: MOCHATIMIT val: 61/61 spans>=3 words occur verbatim in train runs (TIMIT shares sentences); only 2/518 val words are in spans unseen in train. Sherlock1 val 91/192 seen, TheMoth 33/188. Macro selection rewarded memorized word order: ensemble-v1v2 macro 0.542 (> v1 0.504) scored LB 0.310 (< v1 0.385). Novel-span score (val words in spans of >=2 words whose exact label sequence is absent from train; Sherlock n=499, Moth n=980) ranks v1 0.525 > ens 0.496 > v0 0.479, matching LB order v1 0.385 > ens 0.310 ~ v0 0.307. Fix: Split carries a scored mask; macro over Sherlock1+TheMoth on novel words.
close_reason: Landed e06fbeb: Split.novel/Split.seen, Report.novel, macro over domains with >=100 unseen-span words. Ruler ranks v1>ens>v0 like LB.

title: Instrument: seed spread of the v1 recipe on the novel-span ruler

notes: 2026-10-02 v1 recipe seed 1: best ep15 novel macro 0.512 (Sherlock1 0.589 n=499, TheMoth 0.434 n=980; n=1479) vs seed 0 0.525. Same-recipe spread ~0.013 on this ruler; arm must clear ~0.540 to call it.

title: Cross-subject pooling: holdout sentences are identical across all 40 subjects
description: Measured 2026-10-01: subj00_holdout01_sentence has 156 sentences / 155 unique onset patterns (rounded 10 ms, relative to first word); subj01 shares 155 of them. So every Deep sentence has up to 39 other-subject recordings of the same stimulus in the (Broad) holdout files. Transductive lever: match sentences by onset pattern, decode other subjects with a cross-subject model (Broad backbone / subject layer), pool log-probs per word. Plausibly large (averaging many weak decoders). NEEDS HUMAN DECISION: uses other subjects' unlabelled TEST MEG to predict Deep rows - check Kaggle rules (external data / test-data use) before building; private LB 'stimuli entirely different' may or may not repeat across subjects.
notes: 2026-10-02: Deep holdout is subject 0 only (960 rows), spread ratio to train scaler median 1.029 -> cross-subject scaling is Broad-only, not a Deep lever.

title: Down-weight repeated training sentences (repeat_power)
description: v2 showed memorised word order costs ~0.08 on unseen spans; Sherlock sessions repeat text so v1 memorises some. Span sampling weight x count(label sequence)^-p. Test: one run --repeat-power 1 vs v1 novel macro 0.525; bar 0.540.
notes: rp1b (p=1, spans>=3, 20 ep): novel macro 0.535 @ep19 (Sherlock1 0.629 n=499, TheMoth 0.441 n=980) vs v1 0.525: +0.010 directional, < bar; curve still rising at final epoch (v1/v3 decayed) -> less memorisation = later overfit. Ensemble v1+rp1b 0.538 (Sh .628, Moth .449). Not submitted. 30-ep arm context-rp1-e30 launched 00:44Z.
close_reason: No finding. Same mechanism, 3 schedules: rp1b 20ep 0.535, e30 0.507 (@ep15, ends 0.46), v1 baseline 0.525, v3 0.515: run-to-run spread ~0.03 > the delta. Keep opt-in, default p=0. Not ruled out: multi-seed confirmation if a later lever stacks on it.

title: Lever: oversample read-sentence runs (TIMIT 16.8k + MOCHA 0.9k train words = 5.8%)
description: Holdout sentences behave like read sentences (LB 0.307 ~ MOCHA val). Train has TIMIT 14 runs/16,810 words + MOCHATIMIT 2/902 vs 289k narrative. TrainConfig.read_weight scales sampling of those runs; log prior weighted identically. Test: context-v2 --read-weight 4 (~20% read share) vs context-v1 on per-task val, esp. MOCHATIMIT (n=518).
notes: REFUTED for this use (2026-10-01): context-v2 (--read-weight 4, 20 ep) macro 0.502 (MOCHA 0.646 / Sherlock 0.487 / Moth 0.374) but MOCHA val is 100% leaked (every span seen in TIMIT train). Novel-span score v2 0.446 vs v1 0.525 -> oversampling read runs memorises TIMIT sentence order, hurts novel sentences. Does NOT rule out read-domain data helping MEG decoding (isolated-word ctx v2 MOCHA 0.308 vs v1 0.305: flat).
close_reason: Refuted for this use: read-weight 4 dropped novel-span macro 0.525->0.446 (memorised TIMIT prompts). Does not rule out read data used without order (word head).

title: Sentence-context transformer over per-word CNN embeddings
description: 3rd-party rerun: d'Ascoli CNN alone ~chance on holdout, CNN+sentence transformer 0.467. Holdout sentence rows carry every scored word's onset; group windows by sentence (epoch), encode each 1 s window with the CNN, run a transformer over the sequence with onset timing, per-word 50-way head. Train on (run, sentenceidx) groups of vocab words, chunked to <=9. Expected gain: 0.22 -> ~0.45 LB (the rerun's number). Proof: holdout-like val (dense spans) + LB.
notes: context-v0 (44 runs, 131k train words): val context BAcc@10 0.548 (n=1308, epoch-selected; plateau ~0.49-0.50), word head 0.438, dense 0.641 (n=603). cnn-v0 val 0.390. LB public: context-v0 0.30663 vs cnn-v0 0.22128 vs prior 0.200. Big val->LB gap (0.55 vs 0.31) — open question.
